verdict.rationale: FFmpeg's own docs show a one-line conversion (`ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.avi`) and further one-line variants, and the CLI reference is at ffmpeg.html. Community users wrap it in batch files and automated pipelines, which shows it works from scripts, though shell escaping can be painful for complex commands. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of CI usage (exit codes, non-interactive flags) and smoother scripting for complex filter commands.

support.subject: As a developer, a documented command converts a file in one line, usable from scripts and CI

citations.quote: Converting video and audio has never been so easy. $ ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.avi
Force the frame rate of the output file to 24 fps: ffmpeg -i input.avi -r 24 output.mp4
they wrote a batch file wrapper for in/out points and file paths
